proof_summary: Lucas congruences show that for \(0\le m<p-1\) both relevant sums at \(p+m\) vanish modulo \(p\) (pairing the \(k\) and \(p+k\) terms), while at \(p-1\) their values are respectively \(1\) and \((-1)^{(p-1)/2}\), the latter because only the middle term survives. Thus the Hankel matrices are anti-triangular modulo \(p\); reversing the columns contributes sign \((-1)^{(p-1)/2}\), and multiplying the constant anti-diagonal entries gives the two claimed determinant residues.
